Prevention: Clean the field by removing weeds like samajhar ( Echinochloa colona ),to prevent the survival of the bug in alternative hosts.
Select a variety with similar maturity dates commonly used in the area and synchronise rice planting across that area.
Use legume-based crop rotation, if possible.
Conserve natural enemies of the pest, like minute wasps (which parasitize the eggs) and predators like tiger beetles, long-horned grasshoppers, spiders, coccinellid beetles and dragonflies.
Monitoring: Visit the field every 2-3 days to check for the presence of brown-green narrow nymphs and adults feeding on endosperm of rice grains; you may also check for the typical offensive smell.
Yellowing of the leaves, dark grain husk, deformed and spotty grains, brown patches, small and coarse grains and small sized grains.
Attacks are mostly seen upon panicle emergence & milking stage.
Infested paddy straw contains a foul smell.
Take action when 10 or more nymphs or adults per 20 hills are observed.
Direct Control: Use dirty traps including dead crabs or rotten meat in a cloth- pauch @ 1 trap per ropani.
The trap is attached to the top of a stick and firmly fixed in the rice field.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Spray fenvelerate 20% EC @ 2ml per liter of water (25 litres of water per ropani).
Spray cypermethrin 10% EC @1.5 ml per liter of water (25 litres of water per ropani).
